# Results — Study 615 (Yen Safe Haven)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**when stocks crash, the yen rallies**: yen-funded carry trades unwind in risk-off and the
scramble to buy back borrowed yen makes JPY the "free" crash hedge. Sibling of
[69-safe-haven](../../69-safe-haven/) (gold): same folk question, different asset and a
sharper mechanism (positioning, not store-of-value). Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month at build time, 2026-07-03; the partial month is dropped).
Fingerprint `6d34d723338d`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes: `JPY=X` (USD/JPY spot — the yen's return is **minus** the USDJPY change), `SPY` (total-return), `^IRX` (13-week US bill, the carry proxy), `^TNX` (US 10y) |
| Window | 1996-10-30 → 2026-06-30 — **7,418** joint daily returns, **356** complete months (**29.4** years) |
| Labels | JPY is **price-only** spot vs USD (a JPY deposit adds ~0 for nearly the whole sample); SPY is **total-return**; the sleeve's excess return races excess-vs-excess against the US bill |
| Execution | no timing signal anywhere — the hedge is a **static sleeve held in advance** (documented; no lag to apply); event/quintile returns use same-close daily returns, never intraday foresight |
| Survivorship | none — one currency pair + one index ETF, no panel selection |

## The signal — the yen really does move against stocks on bad days

Piecewise daily regression `jpy ~ min(spy,0) + max(spy,0)`, HAC/Newey-West t (10 lags,
plug-in):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| downside beta (SPY down-moves) | **−0.113** · **HAC t = −4.62** |
| upside beta (SPY up-moves) | −0.046 · HAC t = −1.94 |
| unconditional beta | −0.080 · HAC t = −4.45 |
| R² | 0.020 (n = 7,418) |

Quintile ladder — mean JPY return by SPY-day quintile (Q1 = worst SPY days, mean −157.1
bps/day):

| bucket | JPY mean (bps/day) | n |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Q1 (worst SPY days)** | **+12.17** | 1,484 |
| Q2 | −1.35 | 1,483 |
| Q3 | −3.06 | 1,484 |
| Q4 | −4.20 | 1,483 |
| Q5 (best SPY days) | −6.64 | 1,484 |

Welch *t* (Q1 vs Q5) = **+5.81**; Welch *t* (Q1 vs the middle 60%) = **+5.81**. The
conditional flight-to-yen is **decisive on the full tape** — well past the desk's t ≥ 2
bar, with no panel and no survivorship to discount — and it is **not** a two-episode
mirage: it survives dropping every named crash year at once (all six events out, n = 5,924:
HAC *t* = **−4.27**, Welch *t* = +3.97), dropping the 100 worst SPY days (HAC *t* =
**−3.02**, Welch *t* = +4.68), and a 20-seed stationary block-bootstrap (Welch *t* mean
**+5.72**, σ = 0.19, **100%** of seeds > 2). This is a genuine full-sample signal, not a
lucky seed.

**But it has decayed to nothing.** The daily effect is strongly non-stationary — it lives
almost entirely in the first half of the sample:

| era | n days | downside beta | HAC t | Q1 (bps/day) | Welch t (Q1 vs mid) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1996–2010** | 3,529 | **−0.179** | **−6.18** | **+24.04** | **+5.57** |
| **2011–2026** | 3,889 | −0.022 | **−0.89** | −0.83 | +1.03 |
| **2016–2026** | 2,633 | −0.011 | **−0.38** | −0.92 | +0.16 |

The whole "Real" number is carried by 1996–2010. Since 2011 — **half the sample, 15
years** — the daily flight-to-yen is statistically **absent** (Q1 actually pays *negative*),
and since 2016 it is a flat zero. The signal is real in the tape but **gone from the last
decade**: as Japan's rate differential regime and the carry book changed, the reflex
faded. Graded on the full window it clears the bar; graded on a live, forward basis it
does not — hence **Mixed**, not Real.

**But the effect is fast-twitch.** At the *monthly* horizon it evaporates: JPY in SPY
down-months averages **−8.51 bps/mo** (n = 128) vs **−17.16 bps/mo** in up-months
(n = 228) — Welch *t* = **+0.26**, indistinguishable. In the worst-decile SPY months
(n = 35, SPY −7.93%/mo) the yen made just **+0.39%/mo** and rose in only **57%** of them
— a near coin-flip, the same disease as gold's crash record in
[69-safe-haven](../../69-safe-haven/). The yen hedges *days*, not *bear markets*.

## Event studies — 4 hedged, 2 failed (returns computed from the tape; dates hardcoded)

| episode | window | SPY | JPY | verdict |
|---|---|--:|--:|---|
| GFC deleveraging (Lehman → year-end) | 2008-09-12 → 2008-12-31 | −27.43% | **+19.07%** | HEDGED |
| Aug-2015 (CNY deval + flash crash) | 2015-08-10 → 2015-08-25 | −11.07% | **+4.56%** | HEDGED |
| COVID risk-off leg (peak → 03-09) | 2020-02-19 → 2020-03-09 | −18.95% | **+5.75%** | HEDGED |
| COVID dollar scramble (03-09 → trough) | 2020-03-09 → 2020-03-23 | −18.22% | **−5.91%** | FAILED |
| **2022 bear market (top → trough)** | 2022-01-03 → 2022-10-12 | **−24.50%** | **−21.07%** | **FAILED** |
| Aug-2024 carry unwind (BOJ hike → crash) | 2024-07-31 → 2024-08-05 | −6.07% | **+4.87%** | HEDGED |

The classic carry-unwind episodes (2008, 2015, the first COVID leg, Aug-2024) delivered
exactly as the legend says. The two failures share a signature: a **dollar-funding
scramble** (Mar-2020's second leg) and a **rate-shock bear** (2022) — episodes where the
selloff was driven by the *dollar side* of the pair.

## Regime splits — what actually turns the hedge on and off

**A. The carry-stock proxy (US 13w bill ≥ 2% vs ZIRP).** The naive mechanism story — "no
rate differential, no carry stock, no unwind" — does **not** hold:

| regime | n days | downside beta | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| bill ≥ 2% (fat differential, 45% of days) | 3,310 | −0.097 | **−3.83** |
| bill < 2% (ZIRP) | 4,108 | −0.123 | **−3.59** |

The daily flight-to-yen survives in *both* regimes — it is a general risk-off reflex
(safe-haven demand + repatriation), not purely a carry-book artefact.

**B. The operative variable is the yield direction.** Among SPY **down-months**, split by
the sign of the 10-year US yield move:

| configuration | n months | JPY mean |
|---|--:|--:|
| yields FELL (growth scare — differential compressing) | 69 | **+112.53 bps/mo** |
| yields ROSE (rate shock — differential widening all the way down) | 59 | **−150.06 bps/mo** |

Welch *t* of the gap = **+5.14**. The yen hedges **growth scares**, and reliably *loses*
in **rate-shock** selloffs — which is precisely the 2022 configuration (the Fed hiking
into a bear while the BOJ stayed pinned at zero widened the very differential the carry
trade feeds on).

## Tradability — the carry bill eats the hedge

The sleeve is static (held in advance — no signal, no lag; one entry, <1 bp/yr
amortised). Excess-vs-excess: JPY spot minus the US bill the dollars would otherwise
earn, minus an FXY-style 40 bps/yr expense:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| JPY spot vs USD (price-only), annualised | **−2.20%/yr** over 29.4 years |
| minus US bill given up (avg 2.21%/yr): excess | **−4.34%/yr** |
| minus FXY-style expense (40 bps/yr): net | **−4.74%/yr** |

Holding the "free" crash hedge cost **≈ −4.7%/yr net for three decades** — an
equity-risk-premium-sized insurance bill — while its monthly hedge value is statistically
zero (Welch *t* = 0.26) and it *failed outright* in the longest equity bear of the sample
(2022). Retail access is fine (FXY, futures, spot FX) — it is the **negative carry**, not
access, that kills deployment.

## Third axis — 2022: the hedge that failed exactly when needed? **CONFIRMED**

From the SPY top (2022-01-03) to the bear trough (2022-10-12): SPY **−24.50%**, JPY
**−21.07%** — the "hedge" fell **~86%** as much as the thing it was hedging. And the
failure was mechanical, not bad luck: 2022 was a *rate-shock* bear (regime split B), the
one configuration where the carry differential widens during the selloff, so carry got
*more* attractive all the way down. The free crash hedge was absent precisely when the
crash lasted longer than a headline.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful *(never cited for a stamp)*

Deterministic seeded world with a planted crash-hedge knob (`hedge` × |SPY| paid on SPY
down days only):

| planted hedge | downside beta | HAC t | Q1 mean (bps/day) | Welch t (Q1 vs Q5) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | +0.015 | +1.32 | −3.22 | −1.59 |
| 0.30 (planted) | −0.284 | **−25.91** | +45.74 | **+20.75** |

The detector stays flat on the null and lights up on the plant — the real-tape t = −4.62
is a genuine signal, not a construction artefact.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED (real on the full tape, decayed and fast-twitch).** The daily
  conditional flight-to-yen clears the bar decisively over 1996–2026: downside beta
  **−0.113** (HAC *t* = **−4.62**), worst-quintile SPY days pay **+12.17 bps/day** of yen
  (Welch *t* = **+5.81**), no survivorship, and it is robust to dropping every episode and
  to bootstrap — a genuine signal, not a lucky seed. But it is **non-stationary and
  effectively dead**: 1996–2010 carries all of it (HAC *t* = **−6.18**) while 2011–2026 is
  a flat zero (HAC *t* = **−0.89**, Q1 *negative*) and 2016–2026 is deader still (HAC *t* =
  **−0.38**). And even historically it is a *daily/episode* effect only — at the monthly
  horizon the hedge is statistically absent in every era (Welch *t* = 0.26; worst-decile
  months up only 57% of the time). Real in the tape, gone from the last decade.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The always-on sleeve bled **−4.34%/yr excess**
  (**−4.74%/yr** net of expense) for 29.4 years, its monthly hedge value is nil, and it
  failed outright in the 2022 rate-shock bear and the Mar-2020 dollar scramble. The
  negative carry — the exact mirror of the carry trade the legend blames — eats the
  hedge. Not a costs-vs-alpha race you can win by trading less: the bill *is* the
  position.
- **"2022 — the hedge that failed exactly when needed?" — CONFIRMED.** JPY −21.07% while
  SPY −24.50%; mechanically explained by the yield-direction split (growth scares
  +112.5 bps/mo vs rate shocks −150.1 bps/mo among down-months, Welch *t* = +5.14). The
  yen hedges crashes *caused by growth fear*, and 2022's crash was caused by rates.
